title: Manual source review: Byori Python MCP session recovery
task: Explain bounded Python MCP session-loss recovery at the pinned commits: query/login errors, endpoint contracts, and ID precision. Manual committed-source review, not runtime, test-execution, or release evidence.

claims.text: Pinned query mapping: SessionNotFound -> 401 SESSION_EXPIRED; other service errors -> 400 QUERY_ERROR. Permission-check Err yields SessionNotFound; a live-session denial yields AuthFailed. The API table agrees. The MCP docstring's query 403 PERMISSION_DENIED is a documentation discrepancy with this source revision, not runtime evidence.

Query/pin 401 -> login -> USE SPACE -> replace payload.session_id -> replay the ordinary statement. Login clears remembered space. Bare USE/CREATE SPACE are self-pinning exceptions; bootstrap skips the initial automatic pin until ready. Lifecycle source asserts query -> USE -> query, not an executed test result.

Per _raw_query: at most one recovery login and one original-query replay, not recursive retries. Recovery pin/replay HTTPError, including another 401, becomes RuntimeError; failed recovery login propagates. This is separate from startup retries and does not establish safe replay of arbitrary writes.

Client query policy: every 403 surfaces an error without re-login, regardless of body; every 401 triggers session-loss recovery without checking its body code. Lifecycle source asserts 403 rejection. Neither establishes that the pinned server emits query 403.

POST /api/v1/session maps every authenticate error to generic 401 AUTH_FAILED, not stale-query recovery. Client login 401/403 becomes LoginRefused: initial/recovery refusal propagates; bootstrap stops. Client 403/429 handling/comments do not prove those server responses; generic 401 does not identify the refusal cause.

Legacy fallback: 400 retries only when the decoded body contains session, case-insensitively; auth alone is insufficient. This is a whole-body substring heuristic, not structured QUERY_ERROR handling, and can misclassify errors. Pre-0.4.0 behavior is comment/test intent, not independently verified.

HTTP session IDs serialize as decimal strings; query input accepts strings/integers. Preserve the string: JavaScript Number can round large IDs. Python json.loads/json.dumps and unchanged body.session_id carry it into query payloads. This establishes neither precision for all IDs nor out-of-range validation.

/api/v1/query/json returns JSON text with the same 401 SESSION_EXPIRED / 400 QUERY_ERROR mapping. Oversized /query: 413 QUERY_TOO_LARGE; /query/json: plain 413 string. Header-authenticated logout/diagnostics use 401 AUTH_REQUIRED; diagnostics denies live non-admins with 403 FORBIDDEN. Do not automatically extend MCP query recovery to these endpoints.

Manual committed-source/test-assertion review only; no runtime exercised. Blob hashes do not validate semantics, prove tests ran, release inclusion, installed-binary identity, or deployed compatibility. Version-labelled client comments do not override pinned server code.
